record.title: Published claim files carry the gate's raw invocation-path arguments verbatim (${{ github.workspace }}-prefixed in the documented CI usage)
record.description: The publish job republishes each gate run's test.json into public/claims/<artifact>/ (privacy-gate.yml:161, served by upload-pages-artifact at 209-211 and deploy-pages at 213-215) and the same file is uploaded as the gate job's 30-day artifact (privacy-gate.yml:95-104, world-downloadable on this public repository). That summary stores the raw path arguments the gate was invoked with - flow_definition, run_dir and report_file (crates/probe/src/gate.rs:332-364, written verbatim at 365 from PathBufs built straight from the CLI arguments at gate.rs:92/102/105-108; no canonicalisation or relativisation exists anywhere on the path, record.rs:76-79 stores out_dir as given). In the documented CI usage those arguments are built from ${{ github.workspace }} (action.yml:96, 103, 113-119), so the published summary would carry the runner's workspace-prefixed paths - on a GitHub-hosted runner the absolute workspace root /home/runner/work/<repo>/<repo>/... Nothing that consumes a claim needs the prefix: the page renderer never reads test.json (no .rs file in crates/ references it; the index reads report.json and anchor.json, main.rs:682-711), zanary-report verify takes the report path as an argument, and the five recorded data/runs/*/test.json instances only replay the relative arguments their local invocations passed. The same strings also reach the job summary (scripts/ci-summary.py:50, 68) and gate.log (gate.rs:114-115, tee'd at action.yml:120).
record.claimed_root_cause: the summary writer records the CLI path arguments verbatim (definition.display(), outcome.out_dir.display(), outcome.report_path.display(); crates/probe/src/gate.rs:336/337/343) with no normalisation to workspace-relative paths, and the publish step copies that summary into the published claims directory (privacy-gate.yml:161)

trace.scope: composite action (any caller; the caller's workspace value enters the argument strings here)
trace.description: OUT is built as "${{ github.workspace }}/${{ inputs.out }}" and the flow candidate is resolved against ${{ github.workspace }} first (line 96), so both path arguments are workspace-prefixed wherever workspace points
zanary-probe test is invoked with --definition "$FLOW" (114), --out "$OUT" (115) and --summary "$OUT/test.json" (119), so the prefixed strings are the argv values

the machine-readable summary stores flow_definition = definition.display() (336), run_dir = outcome.out_dir.display() (337) and report_file = outcome.report_path.display() (343) - the raw argument strings, no normalisation

cp "$dir"report.json "$dir"anchor.json "$dir"test.json "public/claims/$name/" republishes the summary verbatim as public/claims/zanary-<matrix id>-evidence/test.json, and upload-pages-artifact (209-211) + deploy-pages (213-215) serve it publicly; the same file is also in the job's 30-day artifact (97-104)

evidence.description: render step: zanary-report index --reports claim-input --out public/index.html (154) consumes the run directories; the loop at 158-162 then copies each run's report.json/anchor.json/test.json into public/claims/<artifact>/ (161) - test.json included

gate job: actions/upload-artifact@v4 uploads path: runs/${{ matrix.id }}/ (100) with retention-days: 30 (103) as zanary-${{ matrix.id }}-evidence, so test.json and gate.log are downloadable independently of the Pages site

publish job: actions/download-artifact@v4 with pattern: zanary-*-evidence (140) lands each run's files under claim-input/<artifact-name>/ (141), so the bytes copied at 161 are exactly the gate job's files

recorded instance of the summary: flow_definition "flows/ci-checkout.json" (17), report_file "data/runs/ci-checkout/report.json" (20), run_dir "data/runs/ci-checkout" (22) - the raw arguments this local invocation passed; the file is untracked run output (/data is gitignored, .gitignore:6), and the CI invocation passes the same three fields ${{ github.workspace }}-prefixed

the summary is written to the path given by --summary with the three path fields exactly as displayed (std::fs::write(path, serde_json::to_string_pretty(&summary)?)); the CLI takes them verbatim (92 PathBuf::from(args.require("--definition")?), 102/105-108 for --out) and record.rs:76-79 stores out_dir.to_path_buf() / out_dir.join("report.json") - no canonicalisation, relativisation or workspace check anywhere in crates/probe/src

the job-summary renderer prints the recorded flow_definition (50) and run_dir (68) into $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY (action.yml:139-141), so the same raw strings are also in the job summary and, via the probe's own output (gate.rs:114-115, tee'd at action.yml:120), in the step log and gate.log

blockers: The decisive fact is the runtime value of ${{ github.workspace }}: the action always builds OUT and the flow candidate with that prefix (action.yml:96, 103), but whether it is the absolute hosted-runner workspace (/home/runner/work/<repo>/<repo>) rather than a relative path is GitHub provider behaviour, not repository source. Nothing in the tree settles it - a case-sensitive grep for 'home/runner' over tracked and untracked files returns zero hits, and all five recorded data/runs/*/test.json instances replay relative arguments from local invocations (scratch/ci-private.log:2-3 shows the local recording's 'flow definition : flows/ci-checkout.json' / 'run directory : data/runs/ci-checkout').

The published bytes themselves - the Pages claim file and the 30-day uploaded artifact - are outside this read-only review (no live URL or artifact access; the project's published copy is out of bounds), so the end-to-end observation of the published field values was not made. The copy step is source-verified as verbatim (privacy-gate.yml:161), so what is unresolved is exactly the workspace value above, not the publication path.

No offline execution path reaches the summary writer: zanary-probe test writes test.json only after the flow has run and been verified against the chain (gate.rs:133, 156, 331-368), so replaying the writer with absolute arguments needs the local regtest rig (harness/up.sh - docker plus loopback ports 18232/18233/9067/9068), which a --network=none sandbox and this review may not use.

validation_plan.local: Part 1 (no rig, read-only, already done here): 'grep -rn canonicalize crates/' is empty, gate.rs:92/102/105-108 take the arguments verbatim, record.rs:76-79 stores out_dir as given, and gate.rs:332-364 serialises the three .display() strings - which is why every recorded data/runs/*/test.json replays the invocation strings it was given. Part 2 (needs the documented local rig; non-destructive): with harness/up.sh running (docker + loopback regtest), run './target/release/zanary-probe test --definition "$PWD/flows/ci-checkout.json" --out "$PWD/runs/abs-path-probe" --summary "$PWD/runs/abs-path-probe/test.json" --expect pass' and read runs/abs-path-probe/test.json: flow_definition/run_dir/report_file are expected to be the absolute strings passed in, which settles the writer (not the provider's workspace value). It writes only into the fresh runs/abs-path-probe directory and touches no existing run, claim or wallet state. A unit test in crates/probe/src/gate.rs asserting the three fields are workspace-relative closes the issue permanently.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner-observed, read-only: (1) open one recent 'privacy gate' run on main in the GitHub UI and read the gate step's log or the job summary - both print the recorded fields ('flow definition : ...', 'run directory : ...'; scripts/ci-summary.py:50, 68) - and check whether they start with /home/runner/work/; (2) open the published claim file (for example https://memeshee.github.io/zanary/claims/zanary-private-evidence/test.json) or download the zanary-private-evidence artifact and read flow_definition, run_dir and report_file in it. If those strings are absolute runner paths, the disclosure is confirmed (the same strings are also in the 30-day artifact, the step log and the job summary); if they are relative, this candidate is refuted. Fix: write the three fields relative to the workspace (or to the run directory) in crates/probe/src/gate.rs - that clears every channel - or, at minimum, drop test.json from the public/claims/ copy at privacy-gate.yml:161 and keep it only in the artifact, which only narrows the disclosure.
